concepts.title: Process pairs
concepts.text: A primary and backup run on different CPUs. If the primary fails, the backup can take over. A surviving backup does not mean all CPU capacity is restored.

concepts.title: Takeover
concepts.text: A backup assumes the primary role after failure. Correlate takeover messages with the originating CPU event before opening separate investigations.

concepts.title: CPU loss on NonStop
concepts.text: Redundant processes can continue after a CPU halt while unpaired server processes on that CPU are lost. Check survivor utilization and customer-facing latency.

concepts.title: Pathway server classes
concepts.text: A named group of equivalent server processes serves a workload. Inspect running count, maximum, queue and response time together.

concepts.title: Pathway links
concepts.text: Links connect requesters to server processes. A link-grant failure can indicate unavailable capacity rather than a broken link manager.

concepts.title: NUMSTATIC versus MAXSERVERS
concepts.text: NUMSTATIC keeps a configured floor of static servers. MAXSERVERS limits total instances. A lower static floor can coexist with more running dynamic servers; the floor cannot exceed the ceiling.

concepts.title: TMF audit trails
concepts.text: TMF records transaction changes for recovery. Trail pressure can constrain new work even when CPU utilization is otherwise healthy.

concepts.title: Audit overflow thresholds
concepts.text: TORBANK uses synthetic guards at 80% overflow and 90% begin-transaction disable. These are demo configuration values; read the live trail before proposing action.

concepts.title: N-1 headroom
concepts.text: Ask whether the node can carry its workload after losing one CPU. Baton projects each loss using backup placement and lost server capacity. A risk warning can precede any current service breach.

concepts.title: Reading CPU busy
concepts.text: Utilization shows how occupied a processor is during the measurement interval. Compare survivors, batch placement and service latency; high busy alone does not identify the cause.

concepts.title: EMS collectors
concepts.text: Collectors gather subsystem events into an event log for distribution. Keep event provenance when reducing repeated messages into episodes.

concepts.title: EMS distributors
concepts.text: Printing distributors produce operator-readable event text. Consumer distributors expose events to applications, and forwarding distributors send events to another node.

concepts.title: p95 service latency
concepts.text: 95% of sampled requests complete at or below this value. Compare with the expected calendar band and timeout rate rather than reading the average alone.

concepts.title: Calendar baseline bands
concepts.text: A service band represents expected behavior at this simulated time and load. Black Friday demand differs from an ordinary weekday. A synthetic band is not a production guarantee.

concepts.title: Queues and capacity
concepts.text: A queue forms when offered work exceeds available service capacity. Inspect running versus maximum, CPU load and recent changes to distinguish lost capacity from a configured ceiling.

concepts.title: Protected processes
concepts.text: TORBANK protects PATHMON, disk processes and link managers. A generic suspend request cannot bypass target protection. Use the approved escalation path.

concepts.title: Two-person approval
concepts.text: An impactful T2 change needs distinct approvals and at least one senior operator or expert. The first approval remains visible while the action waits.

concepts.title: Earned autonomy
concepts.text: The trust ledger records outcomes per catalog template, parameter class and role. L2 permits approved read-only automation after an expert grants it; an eligible counter does not grant itself.

concepts.title: Verifying recovery
concepts.text: The CPU-loss scenario requires ATM p95 back within its band for 60 simulated seconds and the hottest CPU below 90%. A single improved sample is not recovery.

concepts.title: Temporary mitigations and undo
concepts.text: Suspending batch and adding static servers buy time. Record inverses, verify service recovery, and retain a follow-up to restore configuration after hardware repair.

glossary.definition: CAIL's desktop and browser 6530 terminal products

glossary.title: Adapter
glossary.text: The single interface through which Baton reads from and acts on a NonStop system
glossary.definition: The single interface through which Baton reads from and acts on a NonStop system

glossary.title: Catalog entry
glossary.text: A vetted command template with typed parameters, tier, undo, parser and citations
glossary.definition: A vetted command template with typed parameters, tier, undo, parser and citations

glossary.title: Check, action
glossary.text: A T0 catalog entry used to gather evidence; a T1 or T2 entry that changes state
glossary.definition: A T0 catalog entry used to gather evidence; a T1 or T2 entry that changes state

glossary.title: Risk tier
glossary.text: T0 read-only, T1 reversible, T2 impactful, T3 destructive (blocked)
glossary.definition: T0 read-only, T1 reversible, T2 impactful, T3 destructive (blocked)

glossary.title: Autonomy level
glossary.text: L0 suggest, L1 run on approval, L2 auto-run read-only, L3 guarded auto-act
glossary.definition: L0 suggest, L1 run on approval, L2 auto-run read-only, L3 guarded auto-act

glossary.title: Trust ledger
glossary.text: The per-template, per-role record of outcomes that drives autonomy
glossary.definition: The per-template, per-role record of outcomes that drives autonomy

glossary.title: Execution token
glossary.text: A single-use permission bound to one rendered command and its approval
glossary.definition: A single-use permission bound to one rendered command and its approval

glossary.title: Fingerprint
glossary.text: The kind of an event: subsystem, event number, component class, template
glossary.definition: The kind of an event: subsystem, event number, component class, template

glossary.title: Episode
glossary.text: A run of same-fingerprint events on one component
glossary.definition: A run of same-fingerprint events on one component

glossary.title: Signal
glossary.text: An anomaly, burst, novelty, threshold crossing or heuristic hit
glossary.definition: An anomaly, burst, novelty, threshold crossing or heuristic hit

glossary.title: Situation
glossary.text: Correlated episodes and signals that an operator should look at as one thing
glossary.definition: Correlated episodes and signals that an operator should look at as one thing

glossary.title: Incident
glossary.text: A situation under structured investigation, with timeline and outcome
glossary.definition: A situation under structured investigation, with timeline and outcome

glossary.title: Origin candidate
glossary.text: The most upstream component with a signal; a starting point, not a diagnosis
glossary.definition: The most upstream component with a signal; a starting point, not a diagnosis

glossary.title: Causal template
glossary.text: A known chain of symptoms used to group and name situations
glossary.definition: A known chain of symptoms used to group and name situations

glossary.title: Failure mode
glossary.text: A library entry with signature, discriminating checks and mitigations
glossary.definition: A library entry with signature, discriminating checks and mitigations

glossary.title: Hypothesis
glossary.text: A candidate cause with a computed score and linked evidence
glossary.definition: A candidate cause with a computed score and linked evidence

glossary.title: Evidence pack
glossary.text: The cited, ranked context given to a model for one answer
glossary.definition: The cited, ranked context given to a model for one answer

glossary.title: Next-best check
glossary.text: The check with the highest information gain per unit of cost
glossary.definition: The check with the highest information gain per unit of cost

glossary.title: Twin
glossary.text: The simulator used to predict the effect of actions
glossary.definition: The simulator used to predict the effect of actions

glossary.title: Claim
glossary.text: One atomic, scoped, reviewable expert statement
glossary.definition: One atomic, scoped, reviewable expert statement

glossary.title: Heuristic
glossary.text: A claim compiled into an executable detector
glossary.definition: A claim compiled into an executable detector

glossary.title: Playbook
glossary.text: A procedure graph of checks, decisions and actions
glossary.definition: A procedure graph of checks, decisions and actions

glossary.title: Shadow session, debrief
glossary.text: Recording an expert at work; the structured interview that follows
glossary.definition: Recording an expert at work; the structured interview that follows

glossary.title: Brief
glossary.text: A narrated summary of system health built from computed facts
glossary.definition: A narrated summary of system health built from computed facts

glossary.title: Card
glossary.text: A streamed UI element: command, hypothesis, evidence, expert, decision, situation, brief
glossary.definition: A streamed UI element: command, hypothesis, evidence, expert, decision, situation, brief

glossary.title: Thread, interrupt
glossary.text: A checkpointed agent conversation or incident; a pause that waits for a person
glossary.definition: A checkpointed agent conversation or incident; a pause that waits for a person

glossary.title: Replay mode
glossary.text: Serving every model call from cache so runs are identical
glossary.definition: Serving every model call from cache so runs are identical

glossary.title: NUMSTATIC
glossary.text: Configured floor of static servers.
glossary.definition: Configured floor of static servers.

glossary.title: MAXSERVERS
glossary.text: Upper bound on server processes in a class.
glossary.definition: Upper bound on server processes in a class.

glossary.title: ATM-AUTH
glossary.text: Synthetic critical server class for ATM authorization.
glossary.definition: Synthetic critical server class for ATM authorization.

operator_messages.text_template: CPU {cpu}, Current State = UP, Previous State = {prev}, Sampling Interval = {n} minutes
operator_messages.cause: CPU monitoring reports an up state.
operator_messages.effect: Processor availability changed.
operator_messages.recovery: Confirm expected recovery and rebalance only after repair.
operator_messages.synthetic_note: Real message identifiers; MVP fallback templates and synthetic brief annotations; state words and simplified layout may be simulated.

operator_messages.text_template: CPU {cpu}, Current State = OVER THRESHOLD, Previous State = {prev}, Current Usage = {usage}, Configured Threshold = {thr}, Sampling Interval = {n} minutes
operator_messages.cause: CPU utilization crossed its configured guard.
operator_messages.effect: Less spare capacity remains.
operator_messages.recovery: Inspect survivor demand and batch work.
operator_messages.synthetic_note: Real message identifiers; MVP fallback templates and synthetic brief annotations; state words and simplified layout may be simulated.

operator_messages.text_template: CPU {cpu}, Current State = FULL, Previous State = {prev}, Current Usage = {usage}, Configured Threshold = {thr}, Sampling Interval = {n} minutes
operator_messages.cause: A CPU is fully occupied.
operator_messages.effect: Services on this CPU may slow.
operator_messages.recovery: Inspect the leading capacity hypothesis.
operator_messages.synthetic_note: Real message identifiers; MVP fallback templates and synthetic brief annotations; state words and simplified layout may be simulated.

operator_messages.text_template: CPU {cpu}, Current State = DOWN, Previous State = {prev}, Sampling Interval = {n} minutes
operator_messages.cause: A monitored CPU is down.
operator_messages.effect: Primaries may take over and unpaired servers may be lost.
operator_messages.recovery: Check survivors; escalate hardware repair.
operator_messages.synthetic_note: Real message identifiers; MVP fallback templates and synthetic brief annotations; state words and simplified layout may be simulated.

operator_messages.text_template: DEVICE ${volume}, Primary CPU Inaccessible, Sampling Interval = {n} minutes
operator_messages.cause: The disk primary CPU is inaccessible.
operator_messages.effect: The surviving backup may continue service.
operator_messages.recovery: Check disk paths; do not restart protected processes.
operator_messages.synthetic_note: Real message identifiers; MVP fallback templates and synthetic brief annotations; state words and simplified layout may be simulated.
